value.account: Cause: from 2.29 (rich loop values) _exhausted_inactive_placeholder_values in orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/control_loops.py materialized a placeholder for every non-scalar inactive-variant field, including relpath fields, and on_exhausted then referenced it; the shared validator forbids on_exhausted overrides of relpath outputs, hence 'may only override scalar repeat_until outputs'. At 2.28 the field was simply left unset on exhaustion. Change: relpath-kind fields are excluded from those placeholders (one condition), so the compiled on_exhausted outputs are identical to 2.28 (verified by diffing compiled debug YAML for the bug's program: status, result__variant, result__rounds, result__question only). Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_path_exhaustion.py compares exhaustion outputs at 2.29/2.32 with 2.28; it fails without the fix. Neighbouring loop/union/rich-loop test modules pass (76). Considered and discarded: letting the validator accept compiler-generated refs for relpath outputs (moves the check ahead of the relpath rejection) - it compiled, but would loosen validation and put a must-exist placeholder path file into the frame, diverging from 2.28. 2.28-and-earlier lowering is untouched since the placeholder path is only taken for rich-loop targets. Not covered: no end-to-end run driving the loop to exhaustion with fake providers (only compile-level equivalence plus dry-run); paths nested inside list/map collections in inactive variants (different contract kind) were not examined; the full suite was not run per instructions.
value.summary: At targets 2.29+ the loop lowering no longer emits an on_exhausted placeholder ref for a path field in an inactive variant, so the program compiles with the same exhaustion outputs as 2.28.

findings: Con Outcome.READY(report: relpath, rounds: Int), Outcome.UNRESOLVED(rounds: Int), :max 1, un continue y :on-exhausted (variant Outcome UNRESOLVED :rounds state.round), 2.28 termina con rounds=2; 2.29 y 2.32 conservan un objeto {ref: ...} como result__rounds y fallan al normalizarlo como entero. Resolver o proyectar esa referencia antes de validar y cubrir la ejecución del agotamiento.
value.summary: La ruta de agotamiento compila, pero una proyección escalar del estado falla en ejecución a partir de 2.29.

value.account: Two root causes. (1) Compile: at 2.29+ _exhausted_inactive_placeholder_values (lowering/control_loops.py) emitted an on_exhausted override for the inactive path field, which the runtime validator rejects ('may only override scalar'); relpath-kind placeholders are now excluded so the inactive path stays unset as at 2.28 (validation untouched, authored path overrides still rejected). That was already in the working tree; I kept it. (2) Runtime, the reviewer's finding: at <=2.28 the match join for the exhausted variant read result field directly from the loop state artifact, while at 2.29+ it reads result__rounds, which on exhaustion holds the compiler-generated {ref: ...state__round} dict, and validate_contract_value rejected it as a non-integer. Fix in orchestrator/workflow/executor.py _resolve_structured_output_artifacts: when the source is a LoopOutputAddress and the raw value is exactly a {ref: str} dict, resolve it through _resolve_ref_value before validation (resolution failure becomes unresolved_output_ref; the resolved value is still validated against the output contract). Tests in tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_path_exhaustion.py: compile-time on_exhausted outputs equal at 2.28/2.29/2.32, and an executed exhaustion run (command-result probe) at 2.28/2.29/2.32 returns UNRESOLVED with rounds=2; it failed at 2.29/2.32 before the executor change. Alternatives discarded: resolving refs in loops.py repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts (cleaner, but tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_recur.py pins the unresolved ref in the loop artifacts, and that would change behaviour at all targets); re-enabling the 2.28 direct state ref for 2.29+ (it is deliberately gated off and the placeholder mechanism depends on it). Verified: 571 passed, 1 pre-existing xfail across loop/exhaustion, rich-loop, lowering, loader-validation, executor-characterization, scoped-union, human-input and strict-boolean modules; did not run the full suite. Not covered: runtime exhaustion with a path value actually active in the exhausted variant, the READY (done) path executed with a real path artifact, and targets 2.30/2.31 explicitly (only 2.29 and 2.32 tested). Nothing committed; bugs/ untouched.
value.summary: Exhausted loops with a path field in another variant now compile at 2.29+ and the exhaustion run returns the same UNRESOLVED/rounds=2 result as 2.28.

findings: executor.py:14910-14920: Un loop/recur válido que termina con Outcome.READY(metadata Map[String,String]) y metadata={"ref":"hello"} falla en el join con unresolved_output_ref porque interpreta el mapa como referencia. Reproducido en 2.28, 2.29 y 2.32; limitar la resolución a las referencias generadas de on_exhausted.
value.summary: La desreferenciación por forma de valor rompe mapas válidos al terminar normalmente y cambia el comportamiento de 2.28.

value.account: Estado: (1) control_loops.py: los campos relpath inactivos ya no reciben placeholder de on_exhausted (el validador runtime los rechaza; quedan sin fijar como antes de 2.29). (2) Se eliminó por completo el hunk del executor.py que resolvía cualquier dict {"ref": str} en el join de LoopOutputAddress (causa del bug reportado: Map[String,String] con {"ref":"hello"} fallaba con unresolved_output_ref). (3) loops.py `repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts`: desde 2.29 (gate con _workflow_version_at_least) las overrides de on_exhausted con forma exacta {"ref": str}, que son siempre generadas por el compilador, se proyectan a su valor en un solo salto (refs al propio frame se leen de los artefactos del frame; las demás con reference_resolver.resolve, sin seguir cadenas); un fallo lanza LoopStateIntegrityError. Antes de 2.29 no cambia nada. Como el valor se resuelve en origen, el join no vuelve a interpretar datos del provider; la salida malformada sigue fallando validate_contract_value. Descartado: filtrar en el join por prefijo de ref o por loop agotado (el valor de un Map ya resuelto podría volver a chocar) y usar _resolve_ref_value (sigue cadenas y reintroduce el bug). Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_path_exhaustion.py (compilación idéntica 2.28 vs 2.29/2.32, ejecución agotada devuelve UNRESOLVED con rounds=2, y Map {"ref":"hello"} intacto en 2.28/2.29/2.32); 8 pasan, más 97 pasan/1 xfail en módulos de loop/exhaustion adyacentes. No cubierto: loops anidados dentro de llamadas donde el nombre del paso en root.steps difiera de step_name (la ref propia no se reconocería y fallaría con error de integridad explícito), ni la suite completa. Sin commit.
value.summary: El hallazgo era correcto: moví la resolución de refs de agotamiento del join del executor al punto donde se construyen los artefactos de agotamiento del loop, así un Map {"ref":"hello"} ya no se interpreta como referencia.

findings: loops.py:724-735: con step_name calificado (por ejemplo call.inner__loop) y ref propia root.steps.inner__loop.artifacts.state__round, la rama de referencia propia no se usa; la resolución sin ámbito falla con LoopStateIntegrityError aunque frame_artifacts contiene el valor final.
